summary.target_audience: Women ages 18-30 who want fresh-looking skin, easy glow, and lightweight skincare that fits into a simple routine.
summary.main_promise: This serum makes skin look more hydrated, fresher, and glowier quickly without feeling heavy.
summary.proof_strategy: Show visible application, fast-absorbing texture, and a clear post-application glow close-up with natural creator reaction.
summary.cta_goal: Encourage the viewer to tap and check out the product.

structure_overview.flow_summary: The storyboard opens with a relatable dull-skin problem, introduces the serum quickly, shows easy application and lightweight feel, delivers a visible glow payoff, then closes with a benefit-linked CTA.

scene_breakdown.viewer_takeaway: This video is about fixing dull-looking skin in a simple, relatable way.
scene_breakdown.visual_description: Creator faces camera in a simple bathroom or bedroom vanity setting with natural light, lightly touching cheek or looking at skin in the mirror before using the product.
scene_breakdown.product_visibility_note: Product is not yet visible; focus stays on the problem state.
scene_breakdown.spoken_line_or_message: If your skin has been looking so dull lately, this is the one thing that’s been helping mine.
scene_breakdown.proof_role: No major proof yet; this scene establishes pain and relevance.
scene_breakdown.transition_note: Quick cut to product reveal so the viewer gets the answer fast.

scene_breakdown.viewer_takeaway: This is the product being recommended, and it fits into a normal daily routine.
scene_breakdown.visual_description: Creator holds the serum bottle close to camera, slightly turning it so the product is clear and recognizable.
scene_breakdown.product_visibility_note: Product should be centered and clearly readable enough to register brand/product type.
scene_breakdown.spoken_line_or_message: It’s this lightweight serum, and I’ve been using it right before makeup or anytime my skin looks tired.
scene_breakdown.proof_role: Begins credibility by framing the product as part of real-life use, not an abstract recommendation.
scene_breakdown.objection_role: Starts reducing the idea that the product is inconvenient or unnecessary.
scene_breakdown.camera_framing: tight product close-up moving into medium creator-plus-product frame
scene_breakdown.camera_motion: small hand-driven motion, natural and casual
scene_breakdown.transition_note: Cut into application while the bottle is still fresh in the viewer’s mind.

scene_breakdown.viewer_takeaway: The serum is easy to apply, sinks in fast, and does not look heavy or sticky.
scene_breakdown.visual_description: Close-up of creator applying the serum to cheek or face, with visible product texture and smooth blending into skin.
scene_breakdown.product_visibility_note: Product should either appear in the hand just before application or remain implied through close-up texture use.
scene_breakdown.spoken_line_or_message: It sinks in really fast and doesn’t leave my skin feeling heavy or sticky.
scene_breakdown.proof_role: This is the first strong proof scene because it shows texture, routine ease, and sensory payoff.
scene_breakdown.objection_role: Directly addresses concern about greasy or uncomfortable feel.
scene_breakdown.camera_framing: tight beauty close-up on skin and product application
scene_breakdown.camera_motion: mostly static or very slight push-in for clarity
scene_breakdown.transition_note: Hold long enough to register texture, then cut to the result reveal.

scene_breakdown.viewer_takeaway: The product creates a visible fresh, hydrated glow almost right away.
scene_breakdown.visual_description: Closer post-application skin shot with creator turning slightly toward light so skin looks naturally glowy, followed by a positive but natural creator expression.
scene_breakdown.product_visibility_note: Product itself can be secondary here; the result on skin is the hero.
scene_breakdown.spoken_line_or_message: It just makes my skin look way more fresh and hydrated almost right away.
scene_breakdown.proof_role: This is the core proof scene showing the benefit the script promises.
scene_breakdown.objection_role: Helps answer whether the product makes a visible enough difference to matter.
scene_breakdown.camera_framing: beauty close-up / slight angle shift to catch skin finish
scene_breakdown.camera_motion: subtle natural movement or micro push-in
scene_breakdown.transition_note: Move from result close-up into final recommendation and CTA.

scene_breakdown.viewer_takeaway: If the viewer wants this same easy glow payoff without a heavy feel, they should click now.
scene_breakdown.visual_description: Creator holds the serum near face or in front of chest while skin result remains visible, finishing with a clean end frame where the product and creator are both readable.
scene_breakdown.product_visibility_note: Product should be clearly visible again in the final shot to reconnect the result to the item being sold.
scene_breakdown.spoken_line_or_message: If you want that easy glow without the heavy feel, tap to check it out.
scene_breakdown.proof_role: The CTA references the exact benefit that was just visually shown, making the ask feel earned.
scene_breakdown.objection_role: Reinforces that the benefit comes without the main downside of heaviness or stickiness.
scene_breakdown.camera_framing: medium close-up with product in frame
scene_breakdown.camera_motion: stable handheld or lightly locked ending frame
scene_breakdown.transition_note: End cleanly on product-plus-result with no unnecessary extra scene.

hook_scene_plan.hook_visual_strategy: Start with a relatable direct-to-camera skin concern in a natural home setting so the viewer immediately understands the problem and feels addressed.
hook_scene_plan.hook_message: Your skin looks dull, and this is what’s been helping.
hook_scene_plan.mute_viewing_support: The creator’s expression plus the overlay text 'Skin looking dull?' helps the opening remain understandable even with sound off.

product_visibility_plan.visibility_priority_note: The viewer must clearly understand that the product is a facial serum and connect it to the glow result.
product_visibility_plan.usage_clarity_note: The application scene should show how little effort is required and how naturally the serum fits into a routine.
product_visibility_plan.repeat_visibility_strategy: Show the product clearly at reveal, imply it through application, then bring it back into the final CTA frame so the product-result link stays strong.

proof_plan.primary_proof_method: creator demo plus visible result close-up
proof_plan.proof_priority_note: The audience must see both the lightweight application and the visible skin finish for the concept to feel believable.
proof_plan.proof_risk_note: If the post-application skin result is too subtle or badly lit, the core promise may feel under-proven.

objection_handling_plan.main_objection: Will it actually make a visible difference without feeling heavy?
secondary_objections: Do I really need another serum?
Will it feel sticky or greasy?
objection_handling_plan.handling_method: Use application texture and creator wording to reduce heaviness concerns, then use the glow result to answer efficacy concerns and reinforce both in the CTA.

overlay_and_subtitle_plan.overlay_strategy: Keep overlays short, benefit-led, and timed to reinforce the most important selling beats without cluttering the frame.
priority_overlay_moments: Scene 5: Tap to check it out
overlay_and_subtitle_plan.density_note: Use one key overlay per scene when possible to keep mobile readability high.
overlay_and_subtitle_plan.avoid_note: Avoid covering the face or product with dense subtitles, and avoid repeating every spoken sentence word-for-word.

fast_moments: Opening movement from pain to solution
pacing_and_transition_plan.transition_style: quick, clean cuts with slightly longer holds on proof scenes
pacing_and_transition_plan.momentum_note: The pacing should move quickly enough to keep retention high, but slow down just enough during demo and result scenes so the viewer can actually register proof.

cta_ending_plan.ending_visual: Creator with visible glow result holding the serum in a clean, readable end frame.
cta_ending_plan.ending_message: If you want that easy glow without the heavy feel, tap to check it out.
cta_ending_plan.action_clarity_note: The viewer should know both what to do and why: tap because the product offers easy glow without the downside of heaviness.

simplification_opportunities: If runtime gets too tight, shorten the product intro line while keeping the bottle reveal.
If production is minimal, use one consistent vanity location and vary only framing, not environments.
production_notes.creator_direction_note: The creator should sound like she is sharing something genuinely useful, not delivering a polished ad read. Light positive surprise is helpful, but avoid overacting.
production_notes.editing_note: Use quick cuts early, then let the proof scenes breathe slightly. Prioritize skin clarity, product readability, and clean scene progression over flashy transitions.
production_notes.generation_note: If this storyboard is later converted to AI generation, keep Scene 3 and Scene 4 especially concrete because they carry the main proof.

assumptions: The creator can film in natural light with enough skin clarity for the result to register on camera.
The serum visually produces enough glow to be noticeable in a short-form beauty close-up.
The product bottle is visually clean and recognizable enough to read well in a close shot.
warnings: If lighting is too flat or too harsh, the result scene may fail to prove the main promise.
If the creator delivery feels too scripted, the UGC credibility of the storyboard will drop.
If the bottle is not shown clearly enough in Scene 2 and Scene 5, product memory may be weaker than benefit memory.
